title: Hope for the Broken
definition: Hope for the broken is the biblical promise that God draws near to the crushed, wounded, sinful, and weary through Jesus Christ.
summary: Brokenness is not beyond the reach of Christ's mercy and restoring power.
christFocus: Jesus came for the weary, the burdened, the sick, the sinful, and the brokenhearted, offering rest and redemption.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Brokenness can come through sin, suffering, trauma, grief, disability, addiction, rejection, or failure. Scripture does not treat broken people as disposable. God is near to the brokenhearted.

Hope for the broken is not based on self-repair. It is grounded in the character of God and the mercy of Christ. Jesus welcomes the weary and gives rest to the burdened.

This hope does not always mean quick change or easy answers. It means brokenness is not the end of the story when Christ is present.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People who feel broken often believe they are beyond help, too damaged to be loved, or too far gone to be used. This doctrine matters because it brings the hope of Christ directly to that lie.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to Christ honestly with your brokenness. Receive His rest, seek support from His people, and take the next faithful step even if healing feels slow.
